svg.text: Scene 0 is the ten-second teaser before Scene 1; it plays the first moment of Scene 1A from standing height on the wall side, and 1A replays it closer, down in the dust.
Black is the dark wool of a hired man's back pressed over the lens; he lunges in at 1.2 s and the white noon floods the frame.
Everyone stands where Scene 1A plan 1 starts, on the shared foreign_farm grid with the tamarisk trunk at the origin.
The smash cut to the hillside lands on the elder son's arm at the top of its draw, the arm the design note asks for.
The younger son is 19 as the screenplay has him; the design note's twelve is older text.
Sun from 270 and high, the white noon of the heading; the wall's short shadow falls north onto the barley, so the road lies in full sun.

svg.text: Frame +x east, +y north, metres, origin the tamarisk trunk; the field wall and its ditch line the north side of the road, the farm lies uphill to the north and the scree falls south from the road's lip to the thorn scrub 45 m out.
Black opens W01 as a hired man's dark back crouched over the lens in the ditch; he lunges aside at 1 s and the white noon floods in.
Four hired men and the two brothers make the dozen hands; HIRED MAN and SECOND MAN speak and the other two stay numbered.
The younger son is 19 as the screenplay has him, and the heel on the hand is his.
The throw rides two whips left, a full turn past the lip and the chasers to the elder son at the wall, then with the stone past the lens onto the runner.
The four FLASH lines are Resolve inserts of about half a second laid over W08's frames, so they add no screen time; W08's does names where each cuts in.
The camera whips over the lip into his eyes as he falls; the cuts to the top and to the foot of the slope are the screenplay's changes of place.
In W12 the camera stands a step down the scree, east of the elder son's eyeline, so he looks down the slope past the lens.
The men's walk back up the road carries their voices into W14, where they fade far away above him.
The shape comes from the south through the thorns, between him and the high noon sun; ELIAB's two blocks share W15 with the eyelids sinking between them.

svg.text: The farm, the house and the valley share one frame, +x east and +y north in metres from the lamp niche in the north gatepost; only the village fire has its own grid.

The house is the owner's one room, 7 by 4 paces (5.25 by 3.0 m) with the hearth FRONT, the doorway RIGHT facing the gate, the sleeping bench BEHIND and the jars and hand mill LEFT, the table at its exact middle.
The niche goes right through the north gatepost, so Eliab lights the lamp from the yard at dusk and sets it back from the road at night, and the flame shows through the house doorway.

The signature move is W20 and W21 in one take, the camera following the lantern out through the gateway between the two sons and stopping in the gateway while the lamp goes down the road into the black valley.
Scene 1A's flash of the old hand cupping the new flame is the middle of W19; Scene 10's flash of the lamp up the black hill with the ewe and the singing comes from W27 and W28.
The ewe handover is the W29 to W30 stitch on her fleece, the camera moving 1.2 m behind it from Asher's shoulder to his front.
W10 cuts to W11 and W27 cuts to W28 on purpose, to fold Asher's walk back to bed and the lantern's long climb into one break each.

Eliab's search goes out by the road, over the valley floor east of the village, up along the black slope to the thorn gully and home up the hill path, so the fire sees his lamp far up the slope behind Asher, about 330 m away.

Amos keeps the night at the threshing floor as at harvest, comes up to the doorway with his sleeves rolled and goes back out to the floor with the bread; Miriam brings the coal because the lamp is lit at every dark.
The midnight meal sits in the doorway's sightline from the fold gate: Micah on a west stool, Eliab pouring beside him, Miriam tearing bread at the table's east side, the dog under the table.

svg.text: The floor is Scene 2's, 9 m across on the terrace's south edge; the brothers winnow with the wind at their backs, the heap just downwind of them, so the grain falls back on the heap and the chaff blows away east over it and down

Asher comes up to him from the farm by the floor track, takes the second fork from the rim stones and works at Amos's left, so in the argument he faces south to the valley and Amos faces north to the house.

The signature move is the whole scene as one designed take circling the brothers counter-clockwise, more than three turns, the toss-together circle outermost (W06) and the words on tighter arcs; when Amos turns back to the wind

Faces are played from the sun side, Amos's from the north-west, Asher's from the south-west, both profiles from the west; every pass behind the heap looks into the low sun with the gold chaff crossing the lens.
Two of the hardest words are played against the low sun on purpose, the first words of W13 in the lane by the heap and the first words of W14 behind it.
Amos turns back to the wind as he does at work, with the wind behind him at the heap, and throws his forkful down the valley the way his brother will go.
The joins hide in the floor's own material, a whip on a gust of chaff (W01-W02), Amos's last forkful drifting into the lens (W07-W08) and Amos's sweat-dark back (W12-W13); the other ten continue.
Asher's invitation in W08 plays on Amos's face as he listens; Asher's three speeches share W12 as in voice test V2, and Amos's accusation and Asher's silence share W13 as in V3.
The other floors lie across the valley about 1.1 km south (eliab_valley farm_across_west and farm_across_east), seen past Amos in W01.

svg.text: The room is the owner's 7 by 4 paces (5.25 by 3.0 m) from eliab_house, unchanged, and the gate lamp shows through the east doorway from the table and the west stools, 34 m away in the north gatepost.

Eliab sits at the head on the north stool with his back to the hearth, Micah at his right hand, Asher beside Micah facing the door and the gate lamp, and Amos at the foot among the hired men, so father and elder son face each

The far end is crowded with five hired men on the sleeping bench, the floor and Asher's mat, and Dan (12) on the mill's reed mat, because the screenplay seats the whole household; everyone keeps their place through the meal, so
the plan draws camera paths only.
The light is one clay lamp on the table and the last grey light from the open door; the hearth is banked under Miriam's pot and gives warmth and breath, and the lamp gives the light.

Signature move, W07 to W12, the camera passes along the open side of the table from Eliab's laugh to Asher's grin to Amos eating in silence, and settles on Amos's jaw at the demand with Asher and Eliab beyond him.
The camera works the open east side between the table and the door, and reaches the west side by walking round the foot of the table among the hired men (W01, W03, W10).
The scene is two long takes, W01 to W11 (94 s) and W12 to W20 (74 s), joined by one bread stitch, Asher's round under his flat hand to Amos's round in his hands, 0.7 m apart.
The Scene 12 flash of the dog trotting off with a round of bread cuts in at that bread stitch, at the end of W11.
After the demand Amos's eyes go up the table to his father, and he drops them to the table when Eliab looks at him first, as the screenplay has it.

W13 and W14 stay at Amos's jaw by choice while the room goes still; insets A and B hold the windows at the foot and the head of the table, and the main map keeps the walks and the signature pass (W07).

svg.text: Scene 1's 33 people keep their numbers, groups and seats; 4A moves Eleazar and Jotham to the wall and Tirzah closer to Hezron, and the teacher turns where he sits to put bread into Hezron's hand.

Eleazar ends outside the wall at (27.7, 2.8) facing the ledge, his hand on the loose stone at the shared anchor (27, 2.6), the pose Scene 16 keeps; Jotham stands beside him at the north gatepost, nearer the gate he steps through
Sun from 140 degrees, low and red over the far hills; the old olive's long shadow lies across the ledge, group A and most of group C, while the wall, the gate and the two men stand in the last sun.
Eleazar leaves the grove's shade for the wall, so the low sun over the wall top lights him from the chest up while he gives the law.
W01 to W03 are one take at the gate; the stitch on his striped mantle hides the seam between his two blocks with the operator in place.
W02 walks behind Jotham and through the open gate on 'the elders at the gate', then turns past the low sun to face Eleazar across the wall top from the gathering's side.
W03 to W04 is a hard cut along the same eastward axis, from the stone under his hand to the stones in the dust by Tirzah; 26 m is beyond a hidden stitch (the 27 m constraint).
Both of Eleazar's blocks run at 2.4 words a second, a lifted voice carried 27 m across the slope.
W03 ends on a chosen near-stillness, the hand on the stone and the stopped stylus, before the cut.
In opening C the law of stoning is what the cold open showed, so the scene ends on bread in Hezron's hand against the stone in Eleazar's.

svg.text: Both hours use Scene 2's farm frame, +x east and +y north in metres from the lamp niche in the north gatepost, with the house door 34 m west on the gateway's axis.
At night Eliab tends the lamp from the road face of the niche, outside his own gate, so Amos comes out across the dark yard to the threshold to speak, and goes back in.
The night wind comes off the hills from the west, down the valley, so the flame leans out of the niche toward the road and holds.
Amos crosses the 34 m in real time, and the camera goes in to meet him and walks backward before him into the lamp's light, a baton pass from father to son and back.
The whip from Amos to his father lands on the answer in place at the post; the other joins inside each hour are continues and one stitch on the papyrus.
The gate and the house door stand open in every frame that reaches them, and Amos goes back in through the open lit door.
The first-light hour opens on the night's last frame, the same lens at the same spot, so one cut carries the hours at the gate.

From the house door the bench sits behind the north post and the 1.7 m wall, so Amos sees the lamp, the gateway and Micah and hears his father, and the lens on the road outside the gateway holds father and son in one deep frame.
Micah walks the south side of the lane so the far doorway stays clear in the deep frames, and stops before the bench with the wax.
The wax passes from Micah's hand to Eliab's, up to the last flame and down to the papyrus in one move, ending on the ring lifting and his hand shaking once.

svg.text: The gate faces north-west up the hill path, the bearing of Eliab's farm; the low sun from 330° puts the square in the shade of the wall and arch and lights the long slope beyond.
The elders sit on the bench at the back of the arched porch, facing out, the door to the village street beside them; Nahum's stool and cloth sit in front of them under the arch.
W01 to W14 is one long take of continues, with Asher's sleeve as a stitch after W04, a whip on the child's laugh after W06 and the stone in Eliab's palm after W08.
Eliab comes over the shoulder of the slope at about 17 s and walks down at about 1.4 m/s; he is small behind Asher in W02 and W04 and grows through the parted lane in W08.
Amos stands at the north-east edge of the crowd from the start, outside every camera field until W14 finds him after the elders' line.
W15 follows a hard cut that skips about 40 s of the climb, so Eliab is already small on the long slope and nears its shoulder by the end; it is the scene's one deliberate break.
The crowd closes behind Asher in the lane and parts again for Eliab; children sit along the wall top on both sides of the arch.
Nahum tips the weighed silver from the pan into Asher's purse while the camera is on the deed and Amos, so W15 opens with the purse already heavy in his hands.

People stand where the plan starts, so Asher is on the path and Eliab beyond the shoulder; the labels Asher and Eliab under the arch mark their places in the trade, and inset A reads the gate where the main map hangs its labels on

svg.text: The farm and the valley share one frame, +x east and +y north in metres from the lamp niche in the north gatepost; the bend is 1.2 km out along the road east at (1040, −580).

Dawn comes straight down the road from the east, so the farewell stands in the bar of first light through the gateway, the father's face lit and the son's back to the sun, and Asher leaves east into the sunrise.

The jenny stands loaded in the gateway's south half; Miriam brings the bread up the lane from the ovens; Eliab steps out of the north post's shadow, the cold lamp in its niche at his shoulder, to bless his son.

W01 to W10 are one take circling father and son, from the jenny's bags past Miriam's bread and behind the son's shoulder to the niche, ending behind the father's shoulder on the road; one stitch on the bread, the rest continues.

The Scene 9 FLASH of the purse and its one coin is a Resolve insert cut into W01 on the stitched bags; Scene 1A's FLASH of a man holding out his own cloak at the bend of a road is taken from W12 at setup S09.

Amos is absent from the gate; he comes down the road after his brother and catches him where the road rounds the last spur of the hill and runs out straight and open to the east, about twenty minutes after dawn.

The sun at the bend is still low in the east (350°), so Asher walks on straight into it; W12 stitches to W13 on the cloak's dark goat-hair wool, and W16 cuts to W17 to fold the minutes until he is a speck about 400 m out.
At dusk Eliab lights the lamp from the yard side of the niche with flint and striker, as at every dark, weeps facing the road through the niche, and turns his back on it to give the order.
Shallum is crossing the yard toward the house, about 15 m off, so the evening order reaches someone; the oxen are in the byre by the north wall.
The blessing is spoken at about 2.1 words a second, so the scene runs about 3.1 minutes against the design note's 2.5.

svg.text: The road east is three small plans with one short window each, joined by hard cuts; the plain beat carries the design note's two big wides, Asher and the jenny tiny on the road and the city lit across the plain.

Kallias's court at night is one stitched long take from the gate to the spilled silver (W04 to W23), the camera passing between diners, cups and faces at couch height, the design note's signature move for Scene 7.

By the owner's map instruction the court is a premium Greek peristyle of 26 columns at 2.9 to 3 m bays, with the open stone shrine of Tyche at the east end and the blazing central brazier on the court axis before her; the gate is
at the west, so the dawn wind out of the east carries her ash over the sleeping couches.

Kallias, Asher and Philon share the head couch facing the goddess, so Kallias writes at Asher's elbow and Asher's arm reaches Philon's neck; Jes sits on the couch edge in the gap before the low table.
Kallias's two opening blocks share W05 with a pause between them; Asher's two blocks around the tablet sit in W10 and W12, with the silent tablet business in W11.
The camera works the high table from five sides (the gap before the couch, both ends of the table, the far side and behind the couch); inset A shows those paths at large scale.
The beggar's corner is outside the gate on its north side, where the company turns up the street, so in Scene 9 the company passes within arm's reach of it on its way in.
At dawn Kallias and the priest are gone and Philon sleeps at the end of the couch; half asleep, Asher speaks at 2.2 words a second and Jes answers as softly.
The dawn and the gate are hard cuts, a time jump and another night; the gate scene ends on the beggar's empty hand.
The west gate square that the design note lists under Scene 7 sits in the screenplay's #8# section, so Scene 8 stages it.

svg.text: Scene 8 plays on the shared farm places in the lamp-niche frame; only the west gate square has its own grid, in the city of Kallias's court.
The montage is two plans and four beats joined by hard cuts, the wheat under the harvest sun and then three rain-dark dusks at the gate lamp and the fold.
The first rain and the winter beat open on the same frame of the gatepost, so the seasons turn at the same lamp.
In the city the last sun comes level through the west gate, so the traveller sees the garland and the stained hem in the only light in the square while the street lamps come on to the east.
The traveller comes on the last day of the wheat harvest, so the gate by day, the lamp at dusk and the fold at night are one day and one evening.

At the gate by day the camera works from the road in the wall's shade, so the trough, the gateway and Amos on the bench share one line of sight and Eliab appears in the sunlit gateway behind the talkers.
At dusk Eliab keeps his face to the road through every line and turns only at the end; the camera reads his face from the road and takes Amos's place in the gateway for Esau's running.
At the fold the camera stays inside among the sheep, so both men's faces come over the wall in the light of Amos's lamp, with the kid between the camera and Amos.
Amos leaves the dusk and the night the same way, walking away inside the yard while his father stays at a lamp.
W30 is chosen stillness, the camera low in the straw through the whole long look at the kid, and the dusk take ends in a slow pull-back down the road.

svg.text: The court, its gate and the beggar's corner are Scene 7's shared place; the rented room and the famine market are drawn here, each on its own grid.

The last feast is one stitched take, W01 to W06, a baton pass that follows the coin from Asher's purse to the wine-seller, past Kallias's stroke to Jes leaving at the gate, then whips back to find Asher.
Scenes 1A and 6B flash the purse tipped over the wine-seller's open palm and the single coin falling, from W01 at about 11.5 to 13.5 s, close at knee height.
Kallias now sits at the west table and Philon on the north-west couch, so the life of the feast has moved to the gate end and Asher drinks alone at the head couch under the lamps he paid for.
Philon's new friend in the court is an unnamed guest; the new boy first appears at the gate, where the screenplay introduces him.

The rented room opens south onto a lodging-house yard, so the noon light through the shutter falls across his face and the landlord stands dark in the door against the white yard, the jenny tethered beyond him.
The famine market runs east to west, so the hot east wind drives the grit down its length toward the opening wide; Asher walks up the street into it and leaves barefoot with it at his back.

The market is one take, W11 to W16; the camera goes down to knee height with each thing he gives up, the cloak, the sandals, the belt with the empty purse, and follows the merchant's eyes to the sling.

At the gate the camera stays low against the wall beside Asher for one take, W17 to W21, turning once up the street with his look and back; in W20, the scene's one chosen stillness, the company's lamps slide across the sleeve over
his face and away through the gate, the design note's signature move.
The shared place draws the gate leaf open; it stands open with the beggar's corner in the post's shadow until the company is in, then the house servant shuts it and the dark comes back.

svg.text: The pig fields are one bare field of rooted dust, about 110 by 64 m inside a low wall of piled field stones, with the three carob troughs in a straight row, the pen, the citizen's booth and fire and one lone carob; its east side
ends in thorn scrub 67 to 72 m from the troughs, the owner's distant thorn scrub boundary.
The men at the estate wall wait in loose knots in the strip of morning shade, and the citizen walks the line beside them in the hard light.
Scene 1A's flash of the pigs at the trough and his own hand drifting toward the husks is the end of W09, over Asher's shoulder into the west trough.
The Scene 2 flash of the lamp coming up the black hill with the ewe across his father's shoulders cuts into W20 at 4.4 s; its source is Scene 2's W27 and W28.

He carries the pig the way his father carried the ewe, across his shoulders with its legs in his fists, and the camera walks ahead of him as Scene 2's W28 walks beside Eliab; the pig's flank is the W16 to W17 stitch, as the ewe's

W15 rhymes Scene 2's signature move, the camera stopping at the trough while Asher goes after the lost one into the dark, as it stopped in the gateway while his father's lamp went down into the black valley.
W17 cuts to W18 on purpose, folding about 70 m of the carry across the black field into one break.

The soliloquy, W23 to W25, is the design note's chosen stillness on the exhausted face, at 2.2 words a second in the faint light of the citizen's low fire; its last 4 s ease back to him alone at the trough under the stars.

Asher sits facing home in the west-south-west and his father looks east down the road; the gate insert opens on the same stars that W21 ends on, and the dog lies at the gate as the design note keeps it there each dark.

svg.text: Thirty-three people in their Scene 1 seats, with Scene 4A's three moves kept exactly; Eleazar at the wall (27.7, 2.8) with his hand on the loose stone, Jotham at the north gatepost (28.25, 1.95), Tirzah pressed close to her father
The small fire burns at the shared anchor fire_sc11_sc16 (3.2, −0.4), between the ledge and groups A and B; Scene 16 uses the same fire, burning low.
Six clay lamps are in hands across the groups (people 7, 11, 16, 22, 27 and 30), each drawn just in front of its holder.
One unbroken take of eight windows with two hidden stitches, the smoothed wax of Jotham's tablet and the flames of the fire.

Jotham's 'Look at the publican' turns the camera and walks it through the gate and 24 m down the open ground to the fire at about 2.5 m/s, the reverse of Scene 1's W14 crossing and the gap Jotham crosses himself in Scene 16.
From the mouth of the gate the north pier hides the loose stone, so Scene 11 keeps Eleazar in profile against the grove and leaves his hand on the stone to Scenes 4A and 16.
Dusk afterglow from about 140°, lower and redder than Scene 1; the Pharisees stand at the edge of the light and the faces at the ledge take the firelight.
The take ends behind the teacher's right shoulder, near Scene 1's S10, with Hezron and Tirzah, the fire and the gate in one frame for 'to Hezron now as much as to the gate'.
Everyone stays seated in Scene 11; the child sits where Scene 1's lizard chase ended.

svg.text: The farm, the edge of the field, the well and the scrub sit on 1A's foreign_farm frame; the two roads west are local grids; the road home sits on Scene 2's eliab_valley frame at road_mile_end (1400, -630), where the road first
comes into view of Eliab's gate.
The farm dog leads the camera up from the reapers to the table and leaves the edge of the field with the bread, so the Sc 4 flash is cut from W12 between 7 and 12 s.
The father's hand rests on the younger son's head from W06 into W09, so Asher sees it from the wall; the cut into W09 is the deliberate break that reveals who has been watching.
Between W09 and W10 Asher slips unseen along the ditch, through the field gap and up the fold's east side behind the oven into the pantry; the cut carries that time.
W11 runs with him as 1A's signature move does, so the theft and the lynching share one running camera, and the barley heads stitch it into the edge of the field.
The elder son reaches the pantry door as Asher bursts out and stays close behind for the whole run; the younger son follows, so both brothers sit down again in W17.
The catch ends at the wall's field face, about 3 m across the stones from 1A's beating on the road side.
The well is staged at noon, later than the morning theft and just after 1A's white-noon beating.
He wakes on 1A's scrub_rest spot with his head 0.4 m west; the scrub windows travel an arm's length at a time, a near-stillness chosen for the exhausted body.
The hired men are 1A's four, numbered 4 to 7; man 7 looks at the ribs and looks away, the same man bent over at the lip in 1A.

svg.text: The farm, the road and the courtyard sit on Scene 2's frame, +x east and +y north in metres from the lamp niche; the run past the village gate sits on Scene 6A's village_gate frame, whose arch and elders' bench replace
The low sun stands at 180° through the whole dusk, between Scene 12's 175° and the farm's 195°, so Eliab runs east with it at his back and comes at his son out of it.
Eliab lights the lamp from the yard face of the niche with flint and striker as in Scene 6B, then steps into the gateway, where the figure shows about 1.1 km down the road below the village.
The evening orders go across the yard by hand and nod, because the screenplay writes them as action; every spoken word in the scene is the screenplay's own.

W01 to W03 is one take that ends at a run behind him down the road under the teacher's voice; W04 follows him down the hill path past the rising elders and stops at its foot by choice while he runs on.

The road comes into the meeting point from 152°, so the runner comes on in the glare just right of the sun and swings straight out of it for his last five metres, where the flare stitch falls, W06 with references off and W07 with

W07 receives the meeting at Asher's left shoulder and turns round them until his arms come up, so the embrace completes inside one window; the name, the confession and the three orders continue in place within two metres.
Micah takes the signet as he turns back, Dan and Shallum run back up the road one order apart, and Miriam stays at Asher's side; the cut to night folds the walk home.
The courtyard plays at the new-lit yard fire before the house door, Scene 14's dance ring, with the gate lamp and the neighbours' lamps far across the yard; the robe's wool is its one stitch.
Amos is away at the far field for the whole scene, as Scene 15 has him; people stand at each plan's start, so slabs and path ends mark where Asher stops dead and where the embrace lands.

svg.text: The room is the owner's 7 by 4 pace shell from places/eliab_house.json, unchanged; the feast fills it and spills out through the RIGHT-wall doorway to the yard fire and the calf's fire (eliab_farm).
Asher sits on the north west stool, which faces the door, so from his seat the doorway frames the yard fire and the gate lamp, and from the gate (Sc 15) the robe shows through the door.
Amos's place is set and empty on the south west stool between Asher and Micah, so Micah speaks of the brother across it.
The drummer and the piper sit on the sleeping bench (BEHIND); the dancers' line weaves in through the doorway, up the table's east side to the hearth and back out to the yard fire.
Eliab brings the best of the calf in from the spit himself, sets it by the untouched bread and goes back into the dancing before the hearth, where Dan finds him in Sc 15.
The camera works from the table's open east side and leans an arm's length over the table for the close faces; the jars, stools and hand mill close the west side.
One long take of nine windows; its one hidden stitch is a dancer's mantle whirling past the lens (W04 to W05), and the rest continue.
It opens low among the stamping feet under the eaves and follows the bread in, and it ends in the doorway looking out past the fire to the gate lamp, the reverse of Amos's view in Sc 15.
The screenplay names only Asher, Eliab, Micah and the dog here, so the household and the neighbours stay unnamed, and an old neighbour eats on the north stool.

svg.text: Scene 11's end state is the start, Scene 1's seats for all 33 and the donkey with Eleazar at the loose stone (27.7, 2.8), Jotham at the north gatepost (28.25, 1.95) and Tirzah pressed close to Hezron (1.15, −0.62); Tirzah now

The light is the fire burning low at fire_sc11_sc16 (3.2, −0.4) and Scene 11's six clay lamps in the hands of people 7, 11, 16, 22, 27 and 30; the gate and the grove lie at the dark edge of it, Scene 15's warm inside and cool
Scene 16 moves two people, Jotham from the gatepost through the gate to a seat beside the shepherd boy, and the boy, who shifts along half a metre toward the olive.

Jotham sets his tablet on the wall top between the north pier and the loose stone, half a metre from Eleazar's hand, then walks round the pier into the open gateway; the gate leaf stands open on the uphill side.
Hezron lays the lead seal on the ground at his knees, between himself and the teacher, in the firelight.

From the ledge Hezron, Tirzah, the fire and the gate lie on one line, so the look past the fire is framed from the teacher's right and the offered bread from behind his left shoulder, where the line to the gate is clear.

Both hard cuts cross the 27 m between the ledge and the gate, on Jotham's look at the seal (W03→W04) and on the offered bread (W07→W08); W04→W05 is stitched on the north pier and W05→W06 on Jotham's back.
The camera walks the whole crossing with Jotham in real time, backward ahead of his face past the D family's lamp, then turning as he passes and hurrying after him into the firelight.
W08 ends the film at Eleazar's shoulder in a chosen stillness, his hand on the stone in front and the offered half loaf small in the firelight 28 m away, then FADE OUT.
Tirzah's one line is set at 2.2 words a second, a child's careful question; the other seven windows are silent and timed by the action.
